stem.text: Water is added to a storage tank at the rate \( r(t) = 9 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{6} \right)} + 9 \) gallons per hour, and removed at the constant rate of 3 gallons per hour, for \( 0 \le t \le 12 \). At time \( t = 0 \) there are 120 gallons of water in the tank, and t is measured in hours. Using a calculator, find the time in \( 0 \le t \le 12 \) at which the amount A(t) of water is greatest, and justify the answer. Show the setup for the calculations.

answer_key.label: The amount is greatest at t = 12, where A is 192 gallons, the largest of the values of A at t = 0, at both critical points and at t = 12.

worked_solution.text: The amount is \( A(t) = 120 + \int_{0}^{t} \left(9 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi s}{6} \right)} + 6\right)\,ds \), so \( A'(t) = r(t) - 3 = 9 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{6} \right)} + 6 \). Setting \( A'(t) = 0 \) and solving with a calculator gives \( t = 4.394 \) and \( t = 7.606 \) in the interval.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical points of an accumulation function

worked_solution.text: The candidates are the critical points and both endpoints: \( A(0) = 120 \), \( A(4.394) \approx 159.174 \), \( A(7.606) \approx 152.826 \), and \( A(12) = 120 + \int_{0}^{12} A'(s)\,ds = 192 \).
The largest candidate value is 192, at the endpoint, so the amount is greatest at \( t = 12 \) hours.
